chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Knowledge is of two types: a knowledge treasured with God which He has not disclosed to anyone from His creation; and a knowledge He taught to His angels and His messengers. As for what He taught His angels and His messengers, it will assuredly come to pass — He does not lie to Himself, nor to His angels, nor to His messengers. And there is a knowledge treasured with Him from which He brings forward what He wills, delays what He wills, and affirms what He wills.'

key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: Bada' — the concept of God's apparent change or revision of decrees; often misunderstood, it actually refers to God manifesting what was previously hidden in His knowledge
key_terms.رُسُل: Messengers/Prophets — those who receive and transmit divine revelation
key_terms.عِلْمٌ مَخْزُونٌ: Treasured/hidden knowledge — the absolute, undisclosed knowledge of God that forms the basis for the doctrine of Bada'
key_terms.مَلَائِكَة: Angels — intermediaries to whom God reveals portions of His will

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about the two types of divine knowledge and bada'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) articulates the doctrine of divine knowledge as twofold: an absolutely hidden, unrevealed knowledge known only to God, and the knowledge shared with angels and prophets which is certain to occur. Within this framework, the Imam introduces the concept of Bada' — God's sovereign capacity to advance, defer, or confirm events from His hidden reservoir of knowledge — without any contradiction to what He has communicated to His messengers. This hadith was transmitted to the early Shia community to clarify the theological basis for believing that God can alter outcomes, grounding this in His omniscience rather than in any inconsistency.
